candidates.change_summary: Remove the ownership check so any caller can trigger the payout.
Invert the ownership check so only non-owners pass the guard.
Transfer zero instead of the full contract balance.
Always send funds to the owner instead of the caller-supplied recipient.
Remove the require(msg.sender == owner) access check so any caller can withdraw.
Change the ownership check from == to !=, inverting who is authorized.
Replace transfer of the full balance with a fixed transfer of 1 wei.
Delete the transfer statement so no funds are sent and the contract balance is unchanged.
Removed the require(msg.sender == owner) check so any caller can withdraw all funds.
Changed the ownership check to require(msg.sender != owner), so only non-owners can trigger the withdrawal.
Changed the transfer amount to a fixed 1 wei instead of the contract's full balance.
Remove the ownership check so anyone can withdraw the contract's balance.
Send a fixed 1 ether instead of the entire contract balance, changing the amount transferred or causing a revert.
Send the balance to the owner instead of the _recipient parameter, changing the destination of the transfer.
Delete the `require(msg.sender == owner);` access-control check so any caller can withdraw.
Invert the ownership check so only non-owners may call withdrawAll.
Send a fixed 1 wei instead of the contract's entire balance.
Redirect the payout to the contract owner instead of the `_recipient` argument.
Replace the transfer of the full contract balance with a transfer of zero.
Delete the transfer statement so no funds are sent to the recipient.
Invert the ownership check so only non-owners can withdraw.
Delete the ownership check so anyone can withdraw the balance.
Remove the owner check so anyone can withdraw the contract balance.
Invert the ownership check so only non-owners may call the withdrawal.
Remove the transfer statement so no funds are sent (the call becomes a no-op).
Replace the full-balance transfer with a transfer of exactly 1 wei.
Replace the full-balance transfer with a zero-value transfer.
Use send instead of transfer so a failed send no longer reverts and execution continues.
Insert a check that the contract balance is nonzero, making calls revert when balance is 0 (originally they succeed).
Remove the require(msg.sender == owner) access control so any caller can withdraw the contract's balance.
Transfer only half of the contract's balance instead of the entire balance.
Change the access control check from owner to always-reverted, so withdrawAll can never succeed.
Insert a zeroing of the owner before transfer so the ownership observable changes after a successful withdrawAll.
Replace transfer of the full balance with a call value of zero so no funds are moved on withdrawAll.
